cover.headline: The best e-scooter brand in India, priced as if it had already won
cover.lead: Ather Energy makes premium electric scooters (450, Rizta and, from Sep-2026, the cheaper Konarc) at Hosur and, from early 2027, at a new 5-lakh-a-year plant at AURIC near Aurangabad. It sold 2,62,942 scooters in FY26 (+69%) for ₹3,672 cr and lost ₹517 cr; in Q1FY27 it reached EBITDA breakeven on its own definition. Demand is running ahead of supply (1.5 lakh pre-orders in Q1, dealer stock 3 days), but its market share slipped to 16-17% as TVS and Bajaj grew faster. The street values the stock on **EV/Sales (5.5-7x Sep-28E or FY29E)**, with no Sell among the eight houses we track (median target ₹1,850). We forecast revenue of ₹6,261 / 9,442 / 11,644 cr for FY27-29E. Applying the house rule, **3.5x Sep-28E revenue of ₹10,543 cr** (the stock's own 12-month forward median of 4.0x, less the auto sector's 10.0% move) plus net cash gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks are lower: DCF ₹465, EV/EBITDA on FY29E ₹341. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Wholesale volumes rose 81% in Q1FY27 to 83,173; registrations +102%. Hosur tops out at ~35,000 a month; AURIC Phase 1 adds 42,000 a month from January 2027 (4-5 month ramp). We model {{F.volume.0|num}} / {{F.volume.1|num}} / {{F.volume.2|num}} scooters in FY27-29E, about 3.3x FY26 by FY29E.

arguments.h: The margin turn has started, but from a low base
arguments.p: EBITDA margin (before other income) improved from −26% in FY25 to −11% in FY26 and −2.7% in Q1FY27 on operating leverage and price rises, despite a 5.6pp commodity hit to gross margin. Konarc lowers revenue per scooter (from ₹99,999) and AURIC adds fixed costs from Q4. We model {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}.

arguments.h: No moat against TVS, Bajaj and Hero yet
arguments.p: Ather's brand, software (94% buy the AtherStack Pro pack) and charging network are real advantages, and its prices are the highest in the segment. But incumbents fund their e-scooters from profitable petrol-bike businesses, and Ather's share fell from 18.6% (Q4FY26) to 15.9% in Aug-2026 while it waited for capacity. Hero MotoCorp, its 30% shareholder, competes with Vida.

arguments.h: Valuation: the price assumes the bull case
arguments.p: At ₹1,425 Ather trades on 5.6x our FY28E and 5.0x Sep-28E revenue, against a 12-month forward median of 4.0x; the multiple more than doubled from ~3x in April to 6.6x in September 2026. P/E cannot be used: FY27E is a loss and FY28E EPS (₹5.9) gives a meaningless ~242x. The street's ₹1,398-2,200 targets rest on 5.5-7x multiples (median 6.25x) that the stock held only in its last two months.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): first full quarter at Hosur's capacity and of June's price rises; whether EBITDA stays positive.
AURIC Phase 1: trial output in the festive season, reliable output from January 2027, 42,000 a month by end-Q4FY27 or early FY28.
Konarc deliveries (phased from mid-Sep-2026; entry variant from Q1 2027) and its effect on Rizta, revenue per scooter and AtherStack Pro attach (guided 75%+).
Monthly Vahan registrations: does Ather regain share once supply improves, or do TVS, Bajaj and Hero keep gaining?
AURIC Phase 2 decision (management: firmer timelines "in a quarter or two"); commodity prices (lithium, copper, aluminium); state EV policies (Delhi, Haryana).

sections.title: One business: premium electric scooters, plus software, charging and accessories that rivals do not match

blocks.p: Ather Energy designs and makes electric scooters and sells them through ~700 franchised experience centres (Mar-2026). It has three families: the **450** (sporty, its first product, 2018), the **Rizta** (a family scooter launched in Apr-2024, now the volume driver: 2 lakh+ sold within 21 months) and the **Konarc** (the first model on its new low-cost EL platform, launched on 29-Aug-2026 from ₹99,999 ex-showroom). It designs the battery packs, motor controllers, vehicle software and dashboards itself and buys cells and most parts. It builds scooters at Hosur (Tamil Nadu; ~35,000 a month, 4.2 lakh a year) and is finishing a second plant at AURIC, Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (Maharashtra; 5 lakh a year in Phase 1, room for another 5 lakh).

What makes it different is the layer around the scooter. **AtherStack Pro**, a paid software pack (navigation, ride modes, theft and crash alerts, over-the-air updates), is bought by 94% of customers; **non-vehicle revenue** (software, accessories, service, charging) was 14% of revenue in Q1FY27. Ather built India's largest two-wheeler fast-charging network (6,000+ points) on its own connector, LECCS, which became an Indian standard used by 20+ companies. Revenue per scooter was ₹1,39,642 in FY26 and ₹1,46,312 in Q1FY27, the highest among mass-market e-scooter makers.

sections.title: Thirteen years, four funding eras: VC, Hero MotoCorp, the IPO and the 2026 top-up

blocks.p: Two IIT Madras graduates, Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain, founded Ather in 2013. Hero MotoCorp invested from 2016 and is now the largest shareholder; GIC, NIIF and others followed. The subsidy cut of 2023 (FAME-II) hit volumes in FY24 and pushed Ather to sell software packs to rebuild margins. The IPO in May-2025 raised ₹2,626 cr of new money at ₹321 a share (plus a ₹355 cr sale by existing holders). In Jul/Aug-2026, with the stock at ~4x the IPO price and demand outrunning supply, Ather raised another ₹2,500 cr to fund AURIC Phase 2 and faster launches.

sections.title: E-scooters went mainstream in 2026: 70% growth, 11% of all two-wheelers

blocks.p: India sold ~21.4 mn two-wheelers in FY26, of which ~1.4 mn were electric (+22%, 6.5% penetration). Then demand jumped: e-2W registrations were 5,25,000 in Q1FY27 (+68%), ~11% of all two-wheelers and ~25% of scooters, and 9,03,420 in Apr-Aug 2026 (+70%). Three things changed at once: the West Asia conflict raised petrol prices and, for the first time, made buyers worry about petrol availability; EV running costs became far cheaper than petrol; and governments pushed harder (Delhi's draft EV policy; PM E-DRIVE extended to Mar-2028).

bullets: **Policy.** PM E-DRIVE (Oct-2024, outlay ₹10,900 cr): e-2W demand subsidy ₹2,500/kWh capped at ₹5,000 a vehicle since Apr-2025; extended in Mar-2026 to 31-Jul-2026, then on 11-Aug-2026 to 31-Mar-2028 with e-2W allocation raised by ~₹1,000 cr to ₹2,767 cr. Delhi's draft EV policy (2026) pushes harder; Haryana following (management, Q1 call). PLI-Auto supports local value addition. Subsidy was 16% of Ather's revenue in FY24, 6% in FY25, 3% in FY26 (AR FY26).

**Fuel.** From early 2026 the West Asia conflict raised petrol prices and caused availability worries; management cites this, plus rising petrol prices, as the main reason e-2W demand jumped (EV searches +75%, Ather searches +118% in Q1FY27).

**Costs.** Two-wheeler commodity index (HSBC / company) +46% over five quarters to Q1FY27: aluminium, copper, plastics (crude), lithium hydroxide +131%; rare-earth magnet export controls by China (2025).

**Outlook.** CRISIL (quoted in AR FY26): e-2W sales of 0.60-0.62 crore units by FY30 and 22-25% penetration. Nomura (10-Sep-2026): 22% e-2W penetration by FY30 (45% in scooters). At FY26's ~2.1 crore two-wheelers, 22-25% penetration means ~45-55 lakh e-2Ws a year by FY30, 3-4x FY26.
**Supply.** Every listed maker was capacity- or supply-constrained in mid-2026; waiting periods of up to two months at Ather (Q1 call). When supply catches up, discounting could return.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the tailwind is real and Ather catches it in volume (+81% wholesale in Q1FY27). But in FY27 it is growing slower than TVS (+92%) and Bajaj (+106%) because it cannot make enough scooters, so the boom so far helps incumbents at least as much as it helps Ather. AURIC from January 2027 is the test.

sections.title: Four big players: TVS and Bajaj lead, Ather third, Ola collapsing, Hero rising

blocks.p: The e-scooter market has consolidated around the petrol incumbents. TVS (iQube) and Bajaj (Chetak) sell through thousands of existing dealers and can price off profitable petrol businesses; Hero MotoCorp's Vida nearly tripled in FY26. Ola Electric, the FY24 leader, lost more than half its volume in FY26 after service problems. Ather is the only independent maker with scale, and the most premium: it is gaining in absolute terms but not in share this year.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** Ather's products and brand are competitive at the top of the market, and Konarc takes it into the ₹1-1.2 lakh segment where TVS, Bajaj and Hero sell most. Hero (30% of Ather) is a shareholder and a rival. We assume Ather holds a 16-19% share of a fast-growing market; regaining the 18-19% of late FY26 needs AURIC on time.

sections.title: Volumes: demand is not the limit, the factory is

blocks.p: Ather dispatched 2,62,942 scooters in FY26 (+69%) and 83,173 in Q1FY27 (+81%), even though April production was only 24,000 (labour shortages, West Asia supply disruption) before reaching 28,000 in May and 31,000 in June. By August Hosur was running at its ~35,000-a-month ceiling. Management estimates it could have sold another 13-15k a month in Q1. The step-up comes from AURIC: equipment installation was finishing in Aug-2026, trial output from the festive season, reliable output from January 2027 and a 4-5 month ramp to 42,000 a month, taking capacity to ~77,000 a month (9.2 lakh a year) by around Q1FY28. AURIC is dedicated to the Konarc/EL platform; Hosur can make up to 18,000 Konarcs a month instead of Rizta if needed.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** FY27E 4,29,989 (+63.5%) is mostly arithmetic: Hosur full for three quarters plus ~37k from AURIC in Q4. FY28E (6,99,979) assumes AURIC is used at ~76% on average and that Ather holds a ~19% share of an e-2W market growing ~45%; Nomura is higher (~7.9 lakh). sections.title: Unit economics: gross margin up 15 points in two years, no longer subsidy-led, but commodities bite

blocks.p: Ather's adjusted gross margin (AGM, revenue less materials, on total income) rose from 9% in FY24 to 19% in FY25 and 24% in FY26; **without the government subsidy it went from 12% in FY25 to 21% in FY26**, because the materials cost per scooter fell 9% in FY26 (₹1,10,199) through design changes (LFP cells, cheaper electronics), supplier localisation and volume. The subsidy is now only ~3% of revenue (16% in FY24), so a further cut would hurt less than it did in 2023. Then commodities turned: the company's index rose 46% in five quarters (lithium hydroxide +131%, copper, aluminium, plastics), costing ~5.6 points of gross margin in Q1FY27 (AGM 22.4% vs 25.4% at the end of Q4). Price rises (ASP ₹1.50 lakh → ₹1.61 lakh by June) and the software pack offset part of it.

pair.title: Revenue per scooter: up with price rises; Konarc will dilute it
Subsidy share of revenue: 16% → 3% in two years

blocks.p: Below gross margin, about three-quarters of costs (staff, marketing, R&D expensed, rent, IT) are fixed (management). Q1FY27 showed the leverage: employee costs fell to 10% of revenue (18% a year earlier) and other expenses to 13% (22%), so EBITDA before other income improved to −2.7% even as gross margin fell. From Q4FY27 AURIC's staff and overheads start, and Konarc's lower prices arrive before its lower costs. ESOP charges (₹58 cr in FY26) are inside employee costs and our margins.

The bulls' 15-20% long-run margin needs both: a recovering gross margin and incumbent-like scale.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: a strong brand and software layer, but no moat yet

verdicts: Premium e-scooter brand: ASP ~₹1.61 lakh (Jun-2026), above TVS, Bajaj and Ola; #1 searched EV brand; Rizta took Ather beyond the south
Pricing power is real today (price rises absorbed in Q1FY27), but demand exceeds supply industry-wide, which flatters everyone's pricing
AtherStack Pro attach 94%; 6,000+ fast chargers on Ather's LECCS standard (now an Indian standard, 20+ members); non-vehicle revenue 14%

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Ather has the best product and software ecosystem among Indian e-scooter makers and the pricing power to show it (ASP ~₹1.61 lakh, 94% software attach). That is an edge, not a moat. Incumbents with ten times Ather's two-wheeler volume, larger dealer and service networks and profitable petrol businesses are growing faster in 2026, and nothing stops them copying features. Ather has not yet earned an operating profit over a full year.

sections.title: Revenue up 100x since FY20; losses halved in FY26 and almost gone in Q1FY27

blocks.p: Ather sold ₹35 cr of scooters in FY20 and ₹3,672 cr in FY26. Growth came in two bursts: FY22-FY23 (the 450X and the FAME-II subsidy) and FY25-FY26 (the Rizta family scooter, launched in Apr-2024, which took Ather beyond the south). FY24 was flat because the subsidy was cut in Jun-2023. Losses peaked at ₹1,060 cr in FY24 (₹885 cr before a one-off charge) and fell to ₹812 cr in FY25 and ₹517 cr in FY26. The EBITDA margin (before other income) went from −40% in FY23 to −11% in FY26 and −2.7% in Q1FY27, as revenue grew faster than fixed costs and the cost of materials per scooter fell 9% in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the improvement is real and mostly operating leverage: management says about three-quarters of the costs below gross margin are fixed, so each extra scooter lifts the margin. But the business has never made an annual operating profit, and FY26 still lost ₹408 cr at the EBITDA level. Other income (₹146 cr in FY26, mostly interest on IPO cash) is what made the company's own "EBITDA" definition look better than Screener's.

sections.title: Cash burn: ₹4,000 cr of equity raised since FY20; free cash flow still negative

blocks.p: Ather has always been funded by equity. Shares issued raised ₹220 cr (FY20), ₹344 cr (FY21), ₹1,200 cr (FY23), ₹901 cr (FY24), ₹87 cr (FY25) and ₹2,540 cr in FY26 (the May-2025 IPO, net of costs), and another ₹2,500 cr in Jul/Aug-2026 (QIP ₹1,300 cr; India Japan Fund ₹200 cr; Hero MotoCorp and founder warrants ₹1,000 cr, of which ₹250 cr paid). Cash used by operations peaked at ₹871 cr in FY23; FY26 was the first year operations made cash (+₹32 cr), helped by ₹268 cr more supplier credit, customer advances and deferred software revenue. Capex rose to ₹506 cr in FY26 (AURIC factory, EL platform).

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** with ~₹4,400 cr of pro forma net cash, Ather is funded for AURIC Phase 1 and most of Phase 2 on our numbers (free cash flow of {{F.fcf.0|num}} / {{F.fcf.1|num}} / {{F.fcf.2|num}} cr in FY27-29E). The risk is not solvency but dilution and returns: equity has been raised every one or two years, and the company has not yet shown it can earn its cost of capital.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts; watch the company's EBITDA definition, capitalised R&D and the GST credit

bullets: **Two EBITDA definitions.** Ather's "EBITDA" adds other income (mostly interest on IPO cash): Q1FY27 was +₹9.5 cr on its measure but −₹33 cr before other income. We use the stricter Screener basis throughout.

**Capitalised development.** Product development is capitalised (intangibles ₹439 cr gross, ₹238 cr under development at Mar-2026, mostly the EL platform) and amortised over ~7 years; R&D spend was ₹448 cr in FY26 (₹345 cr in FY25). Amortisation of EL starts with production in FY27, adding to depreciation.

**Deferred revenue and warranty.** ₹197 cr of software subscriptions and extended battery warranties are booked over time (a conservative feature); warranty provisions were ₹60 cr in FY26 and were recalibrated upward in Q4 for commodity prices.
**Share-based pay** ₹58 cr in FY26 (₹83 cr in FY25), charged in employee costs.
**GST credit** of ₹339 cr sits in current assets because EVs pay 5% GST but many inputs 18-28%; it is recovered through refunds and future output tax.
**FAME-II.** FAME-II/PMP show-cause (29-Mar-2023): Ather agreed to refund off-board charger prices to customers; ₹147.97 cr refunded to Mar-2026, ₹9.81 cr outstanding (deposit held).
**Exceptional item** ₹5.0 cr in FY26: labour codes (gratuity and leave) one-time provision.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unmodified audit opinion, simple structure (tiny overseas subsidiaries), net cash, deferred rather than front-loaded revenue. Two disclosure gaps: no quarterly balance sheet, and Screener's FY26 cash-flow rows are misaligned (we fixed them from the annual report).

sections.title: Net cash of ~₹4,400 cr pro forma; suppliers fund the working capital

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Ather held ₹2,582 cr of cash, bank deposits and liquid funds (₹823 cr cash and bank, ₹552 cr mutual funds, ₹1,207 cr term deposits inside other financial assets, mostly unspent IPO money) against ₹664 cr of borrowings and leases: ₹1,918 cr net. Adding the ₹2,500 cr raised in Jul/Aug-2026 (including the ₹750 cr due when the warrants convert) gives **~₹4,418 cr pro forma, ~₹109 a share** on 40.41 cr fully diluted shares. Working capital is negative (−53 days in FY26, company KPI): trade payables (₹830 cr), customer advances (₹126 cr) and deferred software and extended-warranty revenue (₹197 cr) exceed inventory (₹282 cr) and receivables (₹8 cr). Other current assets include ₹339 cr of GST credit (EVs pay 5% GST on sales but 18-28% on many inputs) and ₹75 cr of subsidy receivable.

blocks.callout: **Pro forma note:** the engine has no share-issue line for industrial companies, so we add the ₹2,500 cr of equity raised after March to the Mar-2026 balance sheet (investments and reserves) and count the 79.4 lakh warrants as shares. Reported Mar-2026 net worth was ₹2,573 cr; shown here as {{A.netWorth.6|num}} cr. See the statement notes.

sections.title: Ownership: Hero MotoCorp 30%, founders 10.7%, Indian funds buying, foreign funds selling

blocks.p: At 30-Jun-2026 the promoter group (Hero MotoCorp and the two founders) held 40.72%: Hero 30.04%, the founders ~5.3% each with their family trusts. Mutual funds held 20.33%, all domestic institutions 29.28% and foreign investors 16.23% (GIC's Caladium 7.56%). Foreign holdings fell from 24% after the IPO as pre-IPO investors sold after their lock-ins; Indian funds bought. QIP (20-Jul) and preferential issue (25-Aug) diluted holders; Hero MotoCorp to ~30.7% on conversion of its warrants (company). Caladium Investment (GIC) sold ~3.05% in the open market on 28-Aug-2026 (market reports of the exchange disclosure; secondary source).

sections.title: Governance: founder-led and transparent, with one unusual conflict: the biggest shareholder is a rival

blocks.p: Eight directors, three independent (AR FY26): Neelam Dhawan (independent chairperson), Kaushik Dutta and Sanjay Nayak (independent); Tarun Mehta (ED & CEO) and Swapnil Jain (ED & CTO); non-executive directors Pankaj Sood, Vivek Anand and Ram Kuppuswamy (COO-manufacturing at Hero MotoCorp, up for re-appointment at the 2026 AGM). CFO Sohil Parekh. Promoters: Hero MotoCorp and the two founders.

verdicts: Statutory auditor's report on FY26 standalone statements unmodified (AR FY26). Simple structure; deferred revenue booked conservatively.
Eight directors, three independent including the chair; three non-executive investor nominees.
Tarun Mehta (CEO) and Swapnil Jain (CTO) have run Ather since 2013 and are buying more (warrants at ₹1,260).

Hero MotoCorp is both the largest shareholder (promoter, 30.0% at Jun-2026) and a direct competitor (Vida e-scooters, 1.44 lakh registrations in FY26). Warrants issued to Hero and the founders at ₹1,260 (25% paid) give them an 18-month option on 79 lakh shares.
Hero gains either way; minority holders need Ather to win share from Vida too.
Share-based pay ₹58 cr in FY26 (₹83 cr FY25), ~1.6% of revenue; ESOP 2025 plan approved; grants continue. Equity raised in FY25, FY26 and FY27.
Dilution has been the price of growth.
FAME-II / PMP show-cause notice (Mar-2023): Ather refunded ₹148 cr of off-board charger prices to customers; ₹9.8 cr outstanding at Mar-2026.
Resolved, but a reminder of subsidy-rule risk.

sections.title: The street: all Buy, targets ₹1,398-2,200 (median ₹1,850), all on EV/Sales

blocks.p: Eight houses published targets between the Q1FY27 results (3-Aug-2026) and our as-of date: Emkay Buy ₹2,200, Axis Capital ₹2,100, Nomura Buy ₹1,926, CLSA Accumulate ₹1,850, JPMorgan Overweight ₹1,850, Nirmal Bang Buy ₹1,538, HSBC Buy ₹1,450 and Ambit ₹1,398: median ₹1,850, +30% vs the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹1,425. A 4-Aug roundup counted 13 Buys and no Sells. Every house that discloses a method uses EV/Sales: Emkay 7x Jun-28E (4-Aug) then 7x Sep-28E (31-Aug); Nomura 5.5x FY29E (10-Sep; 5-7x 'should sustain'); earlier in 2026 Emkay and CLSA 7x FY28E and Nomura 6x (aggregator, Jun-2026). No broker uses P/E: Ather has no profits to multiply. The bulls' case is a structural EV upcycle, Konarc doubling the addressable market, AURIC removing the supply cap and 15-20% long-run margins. The stock rose from ₹1,260 (31-Jul) to ₹1,656 (11-Sep) as targets were raised, then fell 14% into the as-of date.

sections.title: Valuation: 3.5x Sep-28E revenue gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the stock trades at 5.0x

blocks.p: Ather has no earnings to put a P/E on: FY26 EPS was −₹13.5 and we forecast −₹2.1 in FY27E. The house P/E routine (forward P/E median since listing, leaving out loss years) is meaningless here: FY27 is a loss year, and the only "valid" points are Apr-Sep 2026 on our FY28E EPS of ₹5.9, a median of ~192x. So, like every broker, we use **EV/Sales on the revenue the market will look at in September 2027 (Sep-28E: half FY28E, half FY29E)**, plus net cash.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a business we like, at a price that already assumes it wins; SELL

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's most premium e-scooter brand, ~16-17% of a market growing ~70% in 2026, a software and charging ecosystem rivals have not matched, gross margins (21% without subsidy) that no longer depend on Delhi, ~₹4,400 cr of pro forma net cash and a plant that more than doubles capacity from January 2027. Q1FY27 was its first EBITDA-positive quarter on its own measure.

**What you are paying:** ₹1,425 is 5.0x Sep-28E revenue, against a 4.0x median over the past 12 months; the multiple doubled in five months as brokers raised targets. To justify today's price on our 3.5x the company would need Sep-28E revenue of ~₹15,320 cr, ~45% above ours. On the street's method and the house multiple the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): SELL.

bullets: **Rating: SELL, target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).** Our ratings follow the upside to our 12−month target: BUY at +15% or more, HOLD between −5% and +15%, SELL below −5%.
**On today's target we would move to HOLD below ~₹1,060 and to BUY below ~₹880**, or raise the target if AURIC and Konarc deliver volumes and margins above ours.

**This is a multiple call more than an earnings call.** Our revenue is close to the street for FY27 and below Nomura for FY28-29; but even at the street's revenue the house multiple (3.5x) gives far less than the price. The street's median target (₹1,850) implies ~6.7x our Sep-28E revenue.
**Biggest swing factor:** the multiple. Each 0.5x on EV/Sales is ~₹130 a share; each 10% on Sep-28E revenue is ~₹90.

Glossary

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: Electric two-wheeler (scooter or motorcycle); internal-combustion-engine (petrol) vehicle.
Electric two-wheelers as a share of all two-wheelers sold.
Wholesale = dispatches from the factory to dealers (what Ather reports as "units sold"); registrations = vehicles registered on the government Vahan portal (retail sales).
The government's national vehicle-registration database, the usual source for e-2W market shares.
Central-government EV subsidy schemes: FAME-II (2019-24), EMPS (2024), PM E-DRIVE (from Oct-2024; e-2W subsidy ₹5,000 a vehicle, extended to Mar-2028).
Production-linked incentive: payments for local manufacturing of advanced vehicles and components that meet local value-addition rules.
Aurangabad Industrial City in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar, Maharashtra: site of Ather's second plant ("Factory 3.0").
Ather's new low-cost scooter platform and its first model (launched 29-Aug-2026 from ₹99,999).
Ather's paid software pack (navigation, safety and ride features, updates); "attach rate" = share of buyers who take it.
Light Electric Combined Charging System: the charging connector Ather developed, now an Indian standard.
Adjusted gross margin: total income less materials and stock changes, as % of total income (company definition).
Company: profit before tax, interest and depreciation, including other income. Ours (Screener): excluding other income.
Qualified institutional placement: a share sale to institutions. Warrants: rights to buy shares later at a fixed price (here ₹1,260, 25% paid up front, within 18 months).
Enterprise value (market value less net cash) ÷ revenue. Used for loss-making growth companies.
Half of FY28E plus half of FY29E: the 12-month-forward figure the market will look at in September 2027.
How far comparable stocks trade below (or above) their own median P/E over the same window, on the valuation date.
Discounted cash flow valuation; WACC is the required annual return (here the cost of equity, as Ather has net cash).
